Proposition. Littlewood-Richardson coefficient c^\lambda_{\mu u} for Iwahori-Hecke branching

Let \mu \vdash n_1, u \vdash n_2, and \lambda \vdash n_1 + n_2 be partitions. The Littlewood-Richardson coefficient c^\lambda_{\mu u} is the multiplicity of the irreducible Iwahori-Hecke module V_\lambda in the restriction:

  V_\lambda \;\downarrow_{\mathbf{H}_{n_1}(q) \otimes \mathbf{H}_{n_2}(q)} \;=\;  igoplus_{\substack{\mu \vdash n_1 \ 
u \vdash n_2}} c^\lambda_{\mu
u} \cdot (V_\mu  oxtimes V_
u)

Equivalently, c^\lambda_{\mu u} = |\mathrm{LR}(\lambda/\mu, u)| counts the Littlewood-Richardson skew tableaux of shape \lambda/\mu and content u whose reverse-reading word is Yamanouchi (every prefix has \#i \geq \#(i{+}1)).

The coefficient c^\lambda_{\mu u} is a non-negative integer. It is zero if \mu ot\subseteq \lambda or |\lambda| - |\mu| eq | u|.

The LR coefficient gives the multiplicity of V_\lambda in the outer tensor product V_\mu oxtimes V_ u pulled back through the standard inclusion \mathbf{H}_{n_1}(q) \otimes \mathbf{H}_{n_2}(q) \hookrightarrow \mathbf{H}_{n_1 + n_2}(q). This constitutes the Hecke-deformed counterpart of the classical Littlewood-Richardson rule for symmetric groups.

The operator-valued Wenzl 1988 sub-lemma 2.1 (prop:crystal-r-matrix-sub-lemma) sums per (\mu, u) block with multiplicity c^\lambda_{\mu u}:

  \chi^\lambda(W_{\mathrm{inner}} \cdot I \cdot  eta_{\mathrm{block}}) = \sum_{\substack{\mu \vdash n_1 \

The LR coefficient c^\lambda_{\mu u} provides the integer multiplicity consumed by the operator-valued combiner. The operator A^\lambda_{\mu u}(I) acts on the c^\lambda_{\mu u}-dimensional multiplicity space.

The canonical formalism computes c^\lambda_{\mu u} by direct LR-tableau enumeration with Yamanouchi pruning. The canonical A=2,3,4 atomic decompositions rely on precomputed tables. The skew-SYT primitive f^{\lambda/\mu} counts all standard Young tableaux of skew shape and weights all chains. The LR coefficient c^\lambda_{\mu u} counts only the Yamanouchi-valid semistandard Young tableaux of content u.
